analysis.title: "Well, Here We Are": BTIG's Krinsky Says The Nvidia Bounce Is A Gift To Sell As The Dollar Breaks Out
key_insights: BTIG's Krinsky says SPX, NDX and SOX are nearing the end of their recent bounces and expects a move lower into next week. His note is titled "Overhead Supply".

SPX is back above 7,600 after 7,350 a week earlier, a bounce of about 3.8%. It remains below last Thursday's highs, its recent downtrend and the 50 DMA. Krinsky expects the index to stall below the downtrend line near 7,700.
The S&P bounced off its 200 DMA near 7,337, which was Krinsky's target of 7,323 from the prior week. If the bounce fails, the 200 DMA and Krinsky's 7,000 target from last week are the next levels.

Krinsky said last Thursday that rallies back toward 150-155 in SOXX were opportunities to reduce risk, after a confirmed six-month top for semis. SOXX was at $155.30 when the chart was pulled. It could fill its October gap near $169 but BTIG sees little upside beyond that. A close above $175 would make BTIG rethink its cautious stance.

Macro is the main headwind. Krinsky says it has been somewhat forgotten amid Nvidia news. The Bloomberg Dollar Index is breaking out of a multi-year range that has capped every rally since spring 2025.

Goldman's FX team says the rates-led broad dollar rally has taken a number of pairs to new local extremes, with USD/JPY just shy of 160. Japan's FX chief Mimura called the moves excessively rapid, which puts intervention back in focus.

The 2-year Treasury yield posted its biggest two-day jump in over two years after Tuesday's hotter-than-expected CPI. It was about 4.85% when charted, up 11bps on the day, and near the September highs close to 5%. Inflation swaps have not reacted similarly.

Tuesday's CPI was headline +0.4% MoM vs 0.3% expected and core +0.3% vs 0.2% expected. Fed Governor Waller had floated a 50bps hike in December if core came in around 0.3%. Goldman economists added a third Fed hike in March, and the 10Y rose another 10bps to 5.10%.
Bitcoin is down nearly 20% from recent highs and has lost its 200 DMA. Krinsky sees risk back to about 66k from roughly $71,700 on the chart, about 8% lower, which is the top of the June/July base.

Krinsky says the path of least resistance for precious metals remains lower and $3,500 gold still looks likely. He had thought strength in gold miners (GDX) might be a bullish tell, but it did not pan out. Spot gold was about $3,876, below the roughly $4,000 floor that held since last fall and about 30% below the early-2026 record above $5,500.
Goldman's commodity team, in its 2027 outlook, sees gold at $4,650 by December 2027, about 20% above current levels, which contradicts Krinsky's near-term view.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO effective immediately after 33 years, with no succession plan. NVDA opened down 13% and traded about 5% lower by midday per Goldman Market Intelligence, while US stocks traded higher. NVDA fell about 20% in November alone per Goldman.
Upcoming tests are PPI tomorrow and next week's Nvidia earnings, the first without Huang, with the Fed debating a 50bps hike.

tension_points.bull_case: The market has traded well given the Nvidia CEO resignation and its price action. SPX bounced off its 200 DMA and is back above 7,600, and a break above the ~7700 downtrend line would be an impressive statement by the bulls.
tension_points.bear_case: The bounce worked off oversold conditions and leaves SPX below last Thursday's highs, its downtrend and the 50 DMA. Macro headwinds from the dollar breakout and 2-year yields have been overlooked, so the market is vulnerable to another rollover.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close above $175 in SOXX would make BTIG rethink its cautious posture. Getting above the SPX downtrend line near 7700 would also be an impressive statement by the bulls.

tension_points.bear_case: Krinsky says the path of least resistance for precious metals remains lower, with $3,500 likely. Gold has broken below the roughly $4,000 floor that held since last fall.
